raw_response:
I've farmed here 40 years, and chrysanthemum is what I settled on — the price holds up better than wheat-corn rotation on my 35 mu, especially with my well. But 35 mu of flos is a lot of hand-picking work with only me in the household, so I'll have to hire pickers in October.

I buy improved cuttings from the Anguo nursery every 2-3 years — the "Jinsi Huangju" variety does well here and the dealers pay more for the yellow flos. I'll use cuttings I saved from last year's best rows plus buy some new ones, about 4,000 plants per mu.

On fertilizer, I don't skimp. My soil test last year showed phosphorus is adequate but nitrogen runs low by bud stage. I'll apply base fertilizer before transplanting — about 2 bags of compound 15-15-15 per mu (50 kg), then topdress urea twice: once at branching, once before budding. That gives me around 18 kg N, 10 kg P, 10 kg K per mu. I'll add 3 kg/mu potassium sulfate at budding — it helps the flower color hold, and buyers pay attention to color.

Water — I have the well, so I irrigate based on what the plants need, not rainfall. Usually 6 times: after transplant, at branching, before budding, twice during flowering, and one post-harvest if dry.

Pesticide is the headache with flos. Aphids come in June, leaf miners in July, then powdery mildew and rust in August-September. I spray 5 times, rotating chemicals. I stop 30 days before harvest — the Chinese medicine buyers test for residues now, and if you fail the test you lose the whole crop. Not worth saving 50 yuan on one spray.

Tillage: I plough deep in early spring (25 cm) because chrysanthemum roots don't like compacted soil, then rotary before transplanting.

Yield target: 220 kg dry flos per mu. Last three years I averaged 210, 235, 215.
